Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May approving its implementing regulation; Royal Decree-Law 7/2021 of 27 April implementing EU AML requirements and strengthening beneficial-ownership obligations; Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership; Spanish Companies Act, Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July; applicable EU AML legislation, Union restrictive-measures regulations, and customs-control legislation.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A registered office must correspond to the company's real administrative and management address and remain available for official notices. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable for a holding or administrative company only if it provides genuine mail handling, document access, and compliance support. It cannot replace the physical premises required for bonded warehousing, customs control, inventory custody, security, access control, records, and inspection. The company must separately secure an approved customs facility or authorization under the Union Customs Code and Spanish customs procedures. For this business, a virtual office alone is not commercially or regulatory sufficient.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province where the registered office is established, under the coordination of the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada), Articles 19-22 (share capital), 22-31 (incorporation deed and registration), 62 (administrators), and 209 (registered office).

Formation / constitutional filings

Public deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) executed before a notary and filed electronically with the Mercantile Registry via the Colegio de Registradores de la Propiedad, Bienes Muebles y Mercantiles de España.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 29 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada requires a minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid up at formation. Payment must be evidenced by a bank certificate or notarial statement of deposit; no escrow account is required for cash contributions, but non-cash contributions require independent expert valuation report.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety certificate granted by the local municipal technical service or the Fire Services of the Autonomous Community after inspection (basic fire protection measures per CTE DB SI), structural load compliance certificate for the warehouse issued by a competent technician, and occupational safety clearance under Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales, including initial risk assessment, fire drill plan, emergency evacuation plan, and evidence of an occupational health service

Paid-in capital rule: Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada requires a minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid up at formation. Payment must be evidenced by a bank certificate or notarial statement of deposit; no escrow account is required for cash contributions, but non-cash contributions require independent expert valuation report.

At a duly convened meeting of the founding members of Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada ES_SL, it was resolved: (1) the share capital of EUR 3,000 is hereby subscribed and fully paid by the founding partners, and the attached bank certificate of deposit is approved; (2) the registered office is fixed at the address stated in the articles, within the jurisdiction of the relevant Mercantile Registry; (3) the administration is entrusted to a sole administrator, appointed with a five-year term; (4) the administrator is authorised to execute the public deed, apply for the tax identification number, and initiate all operating licences; (5) all prior resolutions are ratified.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); central electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es). Customs, excise and free-zone/bonded warehouse control are administered by the AEAT Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales. Spain is a unitary tax jurisdiction with no sub-central VAT or corporate income tax authorities.

E-government filing portal

An SL must obtain a Spanish tax ID (NIF, in CIF format for legal entities) before formal incorporation: the notary requests a provisional NIF certificate from AEAT; after the deed of incorporation is filed in the Registro Mercantil, the definitive NIF is issued through Form 036/037 using electronic certification. Foreign non-resident shareholders, directors and fiscal representatives must be reported via the same forms. For bonded depot / free-zone operations the SL additionally requires: (i) an EORI number in the format ES + NIF for all customs transactions; (ii) a customs authorization for a free-zone or customs warehouse (Depósito Aduanero) under the Union Customs Code, including an approved storage system and a customs guarantee bond; and (iii) an AEAT electronic certificate (FNMT or qualified provider) for all e-filing, SII transmission and customs EDI/DUA clearance.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SL is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Spanish Corporate Income Tax, Ley 27/2014) at the general rate of 25% (15% for newly created SLs with positive result in the first two tax periods, subject to turnover and activity conditions). Profits are taxed at entity level; shareholders are not treated as transparent. VAT treatment for free-zone and bonded warehouse activities is governed by the territorial and suspension rules of Ley 37/1992 (IVA). — An SL must obtain a Spanish tax ID (NIF, in CIF format for legal entities) before formal incorporation: the notary requests a provisional NIF certificate from AEAT; after the deed of incorporation is filed in the Registro Mercantil, the definitive NIF is issued through Form 036/037 using electronic certification. Foreign non-resident shareholders, directors and fiscal representatives must be reported via the same forms. For bonded depot / free-zone operations the SL additionally requires: (i) an EORI number in the format ES + NIF for all customs transactions; (ii) a customs authorization for a free-zone or customs warehouse (Depósito Aduanero) under the Union Customs Code, including an approved storage system and a customs guarantee bond; and (iii) an AEAT electronic certificate (FNMT or qualified provider) for all e-filing, SII transmission and customs EDI/DUA clearance.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation — the SL is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Spanish Corporate Income Tax, Ley 27/2014) at the general rate of 25% (15% for newly created SLs with positive result in the first two tax periods, subject to turnover and activity conditions). Profits are taxed at entity level; shareholders are not treated as transparent. VAT treatment for free-zone and bonded warehouse activities is governed by the territorial and suspension rules of Ley 37/1992 (IVA).

Available election forms

Spain does not operate a check-the-box or US-style entity classification election. Pass-through treatment is available only for statutorily transparent vehicles such as UTEs (Unión Temporal de Empresas), AIEs (Agrupaciones de Interés Económico) and European EEIGs; an SL cannot elect to be treated as transparent for tax. Relevant elective or special regimes for this profile include: (i) reduced 15% corporate income tax rate for newly incorporated SLs meeting legal thresholds; (ii) optional application of the customs suspensive regime for free zones and bonded warehouses (this is a customs authorization, not an income tax election); (iii) VAT group election for closely linked entities where applicable; (iv) corporate income tax group consolidation election (art. 61 LIS) for groups with at least 70% direct or indirect holding; and (v) statutory hybrid mismatch rules transposing ATAD (Law 11/2021) which disallow elective outcomes that exploit double non-taxation.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

None — registration is mandatory from the first taxable economic activity in Spain, regardless of turnover; any SL or non-resident operator making taxable supplies in Spanish territory must register via Form 036/037 (with prior EORI for customs activities). The simplified VAT regime for small retailers is capped by an annual volume of operations below EUR 250,000 but is not available to free-zone operators, storage providers or customs warehouse operators.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Zero-rated IVA applies to exports of goods to non-EU destinations under art. 21 Ley 37/1992, provided: (i) the goods physically leave EU customs territory within 3 months of the supply; (ii) the supplier retains the status of exporter in the electronic DUA; and (iii) documentary proof of dispatch and destination is maintained. Goods placed in a free zone or bonded depot are outside the scope of Spanish IVA while under the suspensive customs regime (art. 23 Ley IVA); IVA becomes zero-rated at the moment of final export, and the right to deduct input VAT is preserved when the export conditions are substantiated. Services directly connected with the export (loading, handling, storage in the bonded facility, customs clearance and transport) are also zero-rated under art. 21.7 when performed for the non-resident owner of the goods.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA) electronically accepted by AEAT, evidencing the free-zone/bonded-depot exit and the export destination outside the EU
  • Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (with CMR for road exports) proving physical dispatch and arrival in the non-EU destination customs territory
  • Inward Remittance Certificate — bank or payment-provider documentation proving receipt of the export proceeds and compliance with the FX repatriation obligation

Mandatory electronic fiscal reporting and clearance: (i) SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) requires taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million, and VAT groups, to transmit invoice records in XML/API format to AEAT within 4 calendar days of issue (8 days for invoices received via counterparty records); (ii) the Verifactu framework requires billing software to guarantee authenticity and integrity; (iii) Spain has no mechanical digital stamping model for VAT, the fiscal anchor being SII and Verifactu; (iv) Ley 18/2022 ('Crea y Crece') will make B2B electronic invoicing (Facturae / UBL 2.1 format) mandatory on a phased schedule once the implementing regulation enters into force; and (v) all free-zone and bonded-depot customs operations require electronic clearance through AEAT customs EDI/XML systems, with the DUA (Documento Único Administrativo) filed digitally for each import, suspension entry and export movement.

AEAT cross-matches SII invoice records, customs DUA data and bank FX receipts to detect abusive zero-rating. Unsubstantiated export claims trigger: (i) reassessment of undeclared IVA with late-payment interest (interés de demora) and enforcement surcharges (recargo de apremio: 5% ordinary, 10%-20% protested); (ii) penalties under art. 194 LGT for obtaining undue refunds or tax benefits: 50% for serious infringements, 100% for very serious infringements involving false or falsified invoices, and 150% where fraudulent concealment means are used; (iii) loss of input VAT deduction and retrospective clawback within the 4-year statutory assessment window (period is suspended while tax-crime investigations are pending); and (iv) criminal liability under art. 305/305 bis Código Penal for tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000, with imprisonment of 1 to 6 years and fines of up to six times the defrauded amount, plus customs penalty proceedings for false declarations and possible joint liability of directors and legal representatives.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain applies the EU framework for free movement of capital and payments. The euro is fully convertible, and there is generally no exchange-control approval or mandatory conversion for ordinary current-account or capital-account payments. Cross-border dividends, interest, service fees, loan repayments, and capital transactions are not subject to a general Spanish profit-repatriation quota, but remain subject to corporate-law procedures, tax withholding and treaty rules, transfer-pricing requirements where relevant, sanctions, AML controls, and bank documentation. Payments involving non-EU jurisdictions may require additional sanctions, tax, statistical, or bank review. Cash and bearer negotiable instruments crossing EU external borders are subject to applicable EU and Spanish declaration requirements. Spanish residents and payment-service providers may have Banco de España statistical reporting obligations for external transactions; the responsible reporting party and thresholds should be confirmed against current Banco de España rules and the transaction channel.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain has no general statutory deadline requiring export proceeds to be repatriated and no mandatory surrender or conversion ratio. Export receipts may generally be retained in foreign-currency accounts, subject to the company's accounting, tax, AML, sanctions, and any applicable statistical reporting obligations. Retain sales contracts, invoices, transport and customs records, proof of export or customs status, and bank remittance evidence. Exporters should separately assess VAT zero-rating or exemption substantiation and any customs, excise, or bonded-warehouse conditions; customs procedures do not create a general FX surrender obligation.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) is Spain's central bank and participates in the Eurosystem. The European Central Bank sets euro-area monetary policy. The Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT), including its customs authorities, administers customs, tax, and applicable foreign-trade formalities.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium for routine SEPA and supported international payments, subject to the provider's country, currency, sector, and customer acceptance policies. An EU-licensed electronic money institution or payment institution may provide regulated payment services under its authorization and applicable passporting rules, but an EMI account is not automatically a bank deposit, does not necessarily provide deposit-guarantee protection, and may not support capital formation, customs guarantees, trade finance, cash handling, or bonded-warehouse operational needs. An offshore provider without the required EU/Spanish authorization or lawful passporting cannot be assumed to provide regulated services in Spain. Maintain a Spanish bank relationship for tax, customs, payroll, guarantees, and resilient treasury operations.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Opaque ownership, nominee arrangements, trusts, or inability to identify natural-person beneficial owners

Root cause: Opaque ownership, nominee arrangements, trusts, or inability to identify natural-person beneficial owners

Defense evidence: Current ownership chart to natural persons; shareholder register and corporate registry extracts; constitutional documents; beneficial-owner declarations and applicable Spanish beneficial-ownership filings; identity and address evidence; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; explanations and supporting records for any trust, nominee, or intermediary.
Non-resident shareholders or directors, high-risk-country connections, sanctions exposure, or politically exposed persons

Root cause: Non-resident shareholders or directors, high-risk-country connections, sanctions exposure, or politically exposed persons

Defense evidence: Certified identity and address records; tax-residence details; full ownership and control chart; sanctions and PEP screening information; source-of-wealth evidence; transaction rationale; counterparty and country risk assessment; applicable licenses or legal opinions; enhanced due-diligence responses requested by the bank.
Large or unexplained initial capital contribution, third-party funding, shareholder loans, or transfers inconsistent with the business plan

Root cause: Large or unexplained initial capital contribution, third-party funding, shareholder loans, or transfers inconsistent with the business plan

Defense evidence: Executed subscription or shareholder-loan documents; board and shareholder resolutions; originating account statements; proof of beneficial ownership of source accounts; audited or tax records evidencing accumulated funds; funding-flow diagram; payment purpose and accounting treatment; bank transfer confirmations.
Customs-free-zone, bonded-depot, or warehouse activity with unclear authorization, goods origin, counterparties, or payment flows

Root cause: Customs-free-zone, bonded-depot, or warehouse activity with unclear authorization, goods origin, counterparties, or payment flows

Defense evidence: AEAT customs authorization and relevant customs procedure approvals; warehouse or free-zone operator agreements; premises and insurance evidence; customs guarantee details; inventory-control and audit procedures; sample customer and supplier contracts; invoices, transport documents, customs declarations, goods-origin records, sanctions screening controls, and a documented flow of goods and funds.
Cash-intensive operations, unusual payment layering, third-party collections, rapid pass-through transfers, or mismatch between declared turnover and account activity

Root cause: Cash-intensive operations, unusual payment layering, third-party collections, rapid pass-through transfers, or mismatch between declared turnover and account activity

Defense evidence: Expected-volume and transaction-profile schedule; customer and supplier due-diligence files; invoice-to-payment reconciliations; warehouse receipts and inventory records; cash-handling policy; payment authorization matrix; bank-account ownership evidence; explanation and documentary trail for intercompany and third-party payments.
Missing Spanish corporate, tax, or signing-authority documentation

Root cause: Missing Spanish corporate, tax, or signing-authority documentation

Defense evidence: Notarial deed of incorporation and amendments; current Mercantile Registry certificate or extract; Spanish tax identification number (NIF); bylaws; appointment and powers of directors and authorized signatories; board resolutions; beneficial-owner information; registered office evidence; and certified translations, apostilles, or legalization where required.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Route equity through an account held in the investor's or documented funding entity's name to the SL's Spanish bank account, with the transfer reference matching the subscription, capital increase, or shareholder-loan documentation. Obtain corporate approvals and execute the required notarial and Mercantile Registry formalities for capital transactions. Provide the bank with the investor identity and ownership chain, source-of-funds evidence, subscription or loan agreement, resolutions, and intended accounting treatment. Use the correct bank payment-purpose information and any applicable Banco de España statistical reporting classification; there is no universal Spanish FX purpose-code regime for ordinary transfers. Do not characterize debt as equity or use unrelated third-party accounts. For customs guarantees or operational liquidity, arrange a separate facility and confirm acceptable collateral and beneficiary requirements with AEAT and the bank.Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the scheme limits and availability; use SWIFT customer credit transfers, commonly documented through MT103-format information or its ISO 20022 equivalent, for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. Provide accurate beneficiary, bank, invoice, contract, shipment, customs, and payment-purpose details, and retain remittance and reconciliation records. For supplier settlements requiring documentary protection, arrange a documentary commercial letter of credit, documentary collection, or bank guarantee subject to the agreed rules and bank credit approval. Match payment terms to Incoterms, title and risk transfer, customs status, VAT treatment, and warehouse records. Screen counterparties, beneficial owners, vessels, goods, and jurisdictions for sanctions and export-control restrictions before execution.Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards and swaps may be used to hedge documented forecast or committed commercial exposures, subject to the bank's suitability, appropriateness, collateral, and credit requirements.Non-deliverable forwards may be available for currencies subject to local convertibility restrictions, but are not a substitute for checking the relevant jurisdiction's exchange-control rules and must be supported by a legitimate exposure and appropriate bank documentation.Cross-currency and interest-rate swaps may be available for financing or long-term exposure management, subject to documentation, counterparty limits, valuation, collateral, and applicable EU derivatives rules.FX options may be available where the company understands the premium, contingent exposure, and potential accounting consequences; speculative trading should be prohibited or separately authorized by a documented treasury policy.Assess EMIR clearing, reporting, risk-mitigation, and margin requirements as applicable to the instrument and counterparty, together with MiFID II client-classification and conduct requirements. Obtain appropriate master documentation, commonly an ISDA agreement or bank standard terms, and maintain hedge designation and accounting records where hedge accounting is intended.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium for routine SEPA and supported international payments, subject to the provider's country, currency, sector, and customer acceptance policies. An EU-licensed electronic money institution or payment institution may provide regulated payment services under its authorization and applicable passporting rules, but an EMI account is not automatically a bank deposit, does not necessarily provide deposit-guarantee protection, and may not support capital formation, customs guarantees, trade finance, cash handling, or bonded-warehouse operational needs. An offshore provider without the required EU/Spanish authorization or lawful passporting cannot be assumed to provide regulated services in Spain. Maintain a Spanish bank relationship for tax, customs, payroll, guarantees, and resilient treasury operations.

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25%

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19%

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

25 days after end of fiscal year (25 January for calendar year taxpayers)

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 1 - Taxable base Net taxable income after deductions and adjustments Non-residents include worldwide income attributable to Spanish PE or fixed base; file Form 210 for WHT and treaty relief 60 euros per day of delay (maximum 1,800 euros); 1% per month of tax due for late payment
Box 2 - Withholding taxes Withholding taxes on dividends, interest and royalties paid to non-residents Non-residents claim credit for WHT paid on Spanish-source payments 60 euros per day of delay (maximum 1,800 euros); 1% per month of tax due for late payment

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: €250,000

Economic substance scope: Spain enforces Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) under national law and EU DAC6; bonded warehouse operators must demonstrate adequate local employees, premises and core income-generating activities

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion

Statutory sanction: Criminal penalties: fines 100-200% of evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years

Director personal liability: Piercing the corporate veil; directors face personal criminal liability, disqualification and imprisonment
Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalties of 100% of tax adjustment; restitution of evaded tax

Director personal liability: Joint and several liability for tax deficiencies; fines and management disqualification
Withholding Tax Non-Remittance

Statutory sanction: Fines 100-200% of unpaid WHT; possible criminal prosecution

Director personal liability: Personal payment obligation; risk of imprisonment for willful non-compliance
Economic Substance Violation

Statutory sanction: Income recharacterization; loss of bonded warehouse benefits; fines up to €1 million

Director personal liability: Imprisonment for fraudulent conduct; disqualification from directorships
